documents.title: Learning outcomes and teaching approach
documents.text: Example for tutors to replace: By the end of this module, learners should distinguish risk, rates and prevalence; identify cohort, case-control and randomised designs; interpret confidence intervals; explain confounding and selection bias; and reproduce a simple StatsDirect analysis in base R. Begin with a study question and a labelled data table. Ask the learner to explain the denominator and assumptions before calculating.

documents.title: Causal inference — introductory guidance
documents.text: A causal question compares well-defined alternatives in a target population. Observational associations can be distorted by confounding, selection and measurement error. A confounder can be a cause of both exposure and outcome. A mediator lies on a causal pathway; adjusting for it can remove part of a total effect and introduce bias. It does not automatically identify a direct causal effect; direct effects require additional assumptions. A collider is a common consequence; conditioning on it can induce an association. Discuss temporal order and the causal question before selecting adjustment variables.

documents.title: Formative feedback and external review
documents.text: Suggested formative feedback: assess whether the learner identified the population, denominator, time horizon, study design, assumptions and limitations; explain misconceptions; ask a new transfer question. This example pack supplies teaching context only. It does not configure accredited assessment, add scored examination items or authorise a CPD award.
